items.followUp: Define a proposition and give an example of a false proposition.

rubric.why: A proposition is a declarative statement that has a definite truth value.
rubric.description: Defines a proposition as a statement that is either true or false.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as a declarative statement with a truth value.

accept: the sun rises in the east
rubric.why: An example shows the student can identify a proposition.
rubric.description: Gives a suitable example of a proposition.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a clear example that can be judged true or false.

modelAnswer: A proposition is a declarative statement that is either true or false, but not both.

items.followUp: What is the binary number system, and which digits does it use?

rubric.why: The decimal system is defined by its base.
rubric.description: States that the decimal number system has base 10.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the system as base ten.

rubric.why: The digits used are a defining feature of the decimal system.
rubric.description: Identifies the ten digits used in the system.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it uses digits 0 through 9.

modelAnswer: The decimal number system is a base-10 number system.

items.followUp: What is meant by loading a program into main memory?

rubric.why: Loading involves moving stored data or a program from secondary storage.
rubric.description: States that data or a program is transferred from the hard disk.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the hard disk as the source.

rubric.why: The destination of loading is the computer's main memory for use.
rubric.description: Identifies RAM or main memory as the destination.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the data or program is brought into RAM/main memory.

modelAnswer: Hard disk loading is the transfer of data or a program from the hard disk to RAM (main memory).
The data or program is loaded into RAM so that the computer can use it.

items.followUp: What is the Internet? Give one example of a service available through it.

rubric.why: The Internet is commonly defined by how networks are interconnected.
rubric.description: Defines the Internet as a network of networks.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this definition or an equivalent description of interconnected networks.

rubric.description: Gives the Internet as an example of a network of networks.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the Internet.

modelAnswer: A network of networks is a group of interconnected computer networks.

items.followUp: Name two forms of information that may be sent as a message in data communication.

rubric.why: A message is the information being communicated.
rubric.description: Defines a message as information or data to be communicated.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the message as the information/data being sent.

rubric.why: Examples clarify what a message may contain.
rubric.description: Names a valid form of message content.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving at least one valid form, such as text, numbers, pictures, sound or video.

modelAnswer: A message in data communication is the information or data sent from a sender to a receiver.
It may contain text, numbers, pictures, sound or video.

items.followUp: What is the purpose of the file transfer protocol (FTP)?

rubric.why: The answer should identify FTP and its role in transferring files.
rubric.description: Identifies FTP as a protocol used for file transfer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that FTP is a file-transfer protocol.

rubric.why: This describes the file-transfer activity FTP supports.
rubric.description: States that FTP transfers files between computers, including uploading or downloading.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning file transfer between computers or uploading/downloading files.

modelAnswer: File Transfer Protocol (FTP) is a protocol used to transfer files between computers over a network.
It allows files to be uploaded and downloaded.

items.followUp: Why are protocols needed for communication between computers?

rubric.why: Protocols specify rules that communication must follow.
rubric.description: Defines a protocol as a set of rules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a protocol as rules or a set of rules.

rubric.why: Protocols govern communication or data exchange between devices.
rubric.description: Connects the rules to communication between computers or devices.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the rules govern communication/data exchange between devices.

modelAnswer: A protocol is a set of rules for communication between computers or other devices.
These rules control how data is exchanged.

items.followUp: What does a hyperlink do on a web page?

rubric.why: A hyperlink is an interactive link that a user can select.
rubric.description: Identifies a hyperlink as a clickable link or item.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the link can be clicked or selected.

rubric.why: A hyperlink takes the user to a destination.
rubric.description: States that it connects to or opens another page, document or location.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a valid destination.

modelAnswer: A hyperlink is a clickable text or image in a document or web page.
It connects to another web page, document or location.
